questionText: To measure the perimeter of a classroom, which of the following units is suitable?
hints: Perimeter means the distance around something. Which unit measures distance?
Litre measures liquids, kilogram measures weight. What measures length?
Metre is the unit for measuring length and distance.

stepByStep.text: Perimeter = total length around a shape.
Litre = capacity/volume, Kilogram = mass/weight, Metre = length.
So metre is the suitable unit.

misconceptions.B: Only metre measures length — these units are not interchangeable

questionText: To convert decametre to decimetre:
hints: Use the metric ladder: Kilo-Hecto-Deca-UNIT-Deci-Centi-Milli. Count the steps!
Deca is 2 steps above Deci. Moving down the ladder means multiplying by 10 each step.
2 steps down = multiply by 10 × 10 = 100

stepByStep.text: Place on the metric ladder: Deca is above the unit, Deci is below.
Deca to Deci = 2 steps down = multiply by 10 × 10.

misconceptions.B: Divided instead of multiplied (went up the ladder instead of down)

questionText: In which of the following pairs is one unit 1/100 times the other?
hints: 1/100 means one unit is 100 times smaller than the other. Which prefix means 1/100?
'Centi' means 1/100. So centilitre = 1/100 of a litre!
1 centilitre = 1/100 litre. That's the 1/100 relationship.

stepByStep.text: We need a pair where one is exactly 1/100 of the other.
Check each: metre = 1/1000 km (not 1/100). Gram = 1/10 decagram (not 1/100). Kg = 1/1000 tonne (not 1/100).

misconceptions.A: Kilogram is 1/1000 of a tonne, not 1/100
misconceptions.C: Metre is 1/1000 of a kilometre, not 1/100
misconceptions.D: Gram is 1/10 of a decagram, not 1/100

questionText: A shopkeeper has 5.4 kg of rice. He sells 2 kg 750 g. How much rice is left?
hints: Convert both to the same format. 5.4 kg = 5 kg 400 g. 2 kg 750 g stays.
Now subtract: 5 kg 400 g - 2 kg 750 g. The grams part: 400 - 750 is negative! Borrow 1 kg.

stepByStep.text: 400 g < 750 g, so borrow: 4 kg 1400 g
Subtract: 4 kg 1400 g - 2 kg 750 g = 2 kg 650 g

misconceptions.B: Same answer as A, just in decimal (2.65 kg = 2 kg 650 g) — both correct!
misconceptions.C: Subtracted 5.4 - 2.75 but 2 kg 750 g = 2.75 kg, so this gives 2.65 not 2.75
